Member 1 is a 29-year-old community program coordinator at a nonprofit, living with their partner in a rented two-bedroom apartment in a walkable city. They are early-career but established, moderate income, cost-sensitive, and work a hybrid shift schedule, often commuting by public transit. Outwardly they are a high-energy, extraverted ENFJ: cheerful, assertive, talkative in one-on-one settings, community-minded, and consensus-driven. They value family, personal freedom, adventure, tradition, community, spirituality, social status, helping others, and privacy. Their social style is warm but they verify trust and can be emotionally guarded. Internally they carry high anxiety, depression, attachment anxiety and avoidance, and high vulnerability; they manage a chronic condition and a diagnosed attention condition, with mild motion sensitivity. They are tech-comfortable but a late adopter, use Apple devices, Chrome, X and Telegram, prefer text-only communication, pay mostly in cash, and keep three to five subscriptions. They are politically centrist, skeptical of free markets and government regulation, positive on climate action, nuclear energy and new technology, skeptical of renewables, EVs and homeownership, pro-debt, pro-subscription, pro-minimalism and pro-fast fashion, and morally focused on sanctity and liberty rather than fairness. They are cautious about financial and social risks yet change-leaning and adventurous, logical and detail-oriented, often speed-first but quality-focused, always early, and plan only a week ahead. Their habits include daily reading and file backups, weekly inbox-zero and phone-free downtime, weekly re-reading texts, monthly meditation, morning walks, hydration tracking, power-snoozing and skipped breakfasts, and occasional humming or self-talk. They never game or drink alcohol, eat flexitarian, sleep irregularly, exercise monthly, stream little, drink tea rather than coffee, own a dog, and have minimal insurance. At home they are dutiful but not naturally orderly, which can clash with a tidier partner.

Member 2 is a 31-year-old arts administrator and freelance illustrator, living with Member 1 in the same rented city apartment. They are a strongly extroverted, novelty-seeking ENFP: excited, cheerful, competitive, big-group-loving, intuition-led, and driven by autonomy, achievement, creativity, status, independence, health and helping others. They are devout, apolitical, spiritually grounded, and possess a signature sense of perspective and appreciation of beauty; they love learning, leadership and open-minded exploration. At the same time they have high neuroticism, high depression and attachment anxiety, and their mental health is struggling; they are risk-averse in high-stakes medical, legal and financial matters, with very low ethical risk tolerance, yet they are an excitement-seeker who is risk-enthusiast in abstract attitudes and an early adopter of some ideas despite being tech-avoidant. They work a remote-leaning 9-to-5 but also value working from the office; they usually drive, cook daily, are tidy, night-owl, high-caffeine, time-late, and run on weekly planning. They are cost-sensitive and a frugal saver on fixed costs but a free spender and impulse buyer for experiences, with a traditional bank, cash preference, zero to two subscriptions, YouTube and WhatsApp, mixed devices and Chrome. Their diet is omnivore with a medical restriction; they have reduced manual dexterity, mild attention and motion sensitivity, very high health literacy and comprehensive insurance. They value health, power and influence, achievement, creativity and self-expression, social status, independence and helping others, with very high benevolence and strong autonomy, competence and relatedness needs. Politically they are apolitical but lean pro-free-market and pro-regulation, skeptical of climate action, data privacy and new technology, positive on nuclear energy, homeownership, risk-taking, subscriptions, working from office and EVs, and skeptical of consumerism, fast fashion, urban density and climate action. Their daily habits include daily stretching, weekly budget tracking, weekly reading before bed, weekly power-snoozing, late-night snacking, doomscrolling, talking to oneself and file backups, plus monthly cold showers, meditation and reflection; they never meal-prep, never track hydration, never practice gratitude, never keep inbox-zero, never re-read texts, and never volunteer or give to charity. They are the tidier partner, but their irregular late-night energy and high emotional intensity make shared routines a negotiation.
